description: Enhance allocation algorithm to include 'Partially Fulfilled' requests alongside 'Pending' requests in allocation runs, allocating against remaining demand (quantity - total_received) rather than original quantity, while preserving the existing priority scoring (45% urgency + 30% severity + 25% people affected)
steps: 1. Update pending_requests() helper in app.py to include requests with status IN ('Pending', 'Partially Fulfilled') instead of only 'Pending'. Sort by id to maintain consistent ordering.
2. Modify the query in pending_requests() to compute remaining_demand = quantity - total_received for each request, and include it in the returned dict.

3. Update allocations route in app.py to pass remaining_demand (not quantity) to the allocate() function. The request dict passed to allocate() should have quantity field set to remaining_demand for partially fulfilled requests.

4. Update finalize_request() logic: when a 'Partially Fulfilled' request receives another allocation, add the new allocation to total_allocated (already done in FEAT-001), create a new delivery, and keep status as 'Partially Fulfilled' until remaining demand reaches 0.

5. Update allocations.html template to show both 'Requested' (original quantity) and 'Remaining' columns when displaying partially fulfilled requests. Add a pill to indicate which requests are being reallocated.

6. Test reallocation flow: apply initial allocation that partially fulfills a request, receive new stock via /admin/inventory, run allocation again, and verify the partially fulfilled request appears in the plan with its remaining demand.
acceptance_criteria: pending_requests() returns both 'Pending' and 'Partially Fulfilled' requests
Allocation algorithm allocates against remaining demand (quantity - total_received), not original quantity
Priority scoring remains unchanged: 45% urgency + 30% severity + 25% people affected
A request can receive multiple allocations over time without losing track of what's already been allocated
allocations.html template clearly shows which requests are being reallocated and their remaining demand
verification: Delete reliefgrid.db and run python app.py
Login as admin, navigate to /admin/allocations, apply allocation (some requests will be partially fulfilled due to limited stock)
Add new stock via /admin/inventory (receive 100 units of Drinking Water)
Navigate back to /admin/allocations and verify partially fulfilled requests appear in the plan with their remaining demand amount
Apply the reallocation and verify deliveries are created correctly
